Water clarity measures how much light penetrates the water column. The
amount of light reaching the seafloor affects the condition and species
composition of submerged aquatic vegetation which need sunlight for
productivity. Some seagrasses can even directly improve local water
clarity by absorbing dissolved nutrients and trapping sediment particles
in their blades and roots. Several parameters can affect water clarity
including turbidity, total suspended solids, and the concentrations of
chlorophyll a and colored dissolved organic matter. A few of the
instruments used to quantify water clarity for monitoring submerged
aquatic vegetation are Secchi disks and turbidity meters.
